factualSource.title: STANLEY: Why does the hook on the end of the Stanley tape rule move?
factualSource.supports: Hook travel compensates thickness; outside measurement pulls and inside measurement pushes. Does not supply manufacturing dimensions.

contactTerminologyResolution.labelMeaning: INSIDE/OUTSIDE label the hook face in shots6/7, not measurement mode. They are not swapped when measurementMode outside/inside is introduced.
contactTerminologyResolution.rigTransitions: Source q runs from h to0 when pulled and0 to h when pushed; root translation keeps the chosen contact face at x0 throughout the contact demonstration. Use named states, not inferred label text.
contactTerminologyResolution.referenceFieldPolicy: selectedContactFace is null or a physical inner/outer hook face; proofTarget independently names annotation/camera/detail targets. Return context retains outside measurement contact with hook.innerFace while camera proofTarget is housing.center.

modelSimplifications: Unbranded generic tape measure, authored dimensions in explanatory units; hook thickness h=.18 and travel h are conceptual, not manufacturing measurements.
No CAD, real tolerance, force/contact simulation, material certification or general collision detection.
Two rivets/slot forms are authored original geometry; rivets are children of fixed model, hook flange is the moving group.
Blade is procedurally curved with z=1.91+.075*(1-y*y) and a thin backing box; doubled-sided blade material is a source modeling choice.
Rounded flange extrusion provides real through-slots and bevels; front hook, fold transition and housing are authored generic solid shapes.
Wood grain and tape digits are generated procedural textures; studio RoomEnvironment is a library scene, not a licensed customer photographic environment.
Source slots/clearance/contact tests are analytic model checks, not mechanical certification.
Each shot uses intentionally authored camera views/cuts; no general auto-framing or reusable camera compiler is present in historical scripts.
